newsitem.title: USA: "Marlboro people" protest at Morris annual meeting.
newsitem.headline: "Marlboro people" protest at Morris annual meeting.

text.p: Protesters costumed as Marlboro cigarettes on Thursday greeted shareholders arriving for Philip Morris Cos Inc's annual meeting at the company's biggest tobacco manufacturing plant.

"Shame on Philip Morris," read signs carried by the 20 or so protestors organized by INFACT, a Boston-based activist group which says Philip Morris, the tobacco and food giant, uses its large lobbying force to harm public health.
Marlboro is Philip Morris' best-known brand, and the company has about a 50 percent share of the U.S. cigarette market.
Other protestors at the front gates to the 45-acre plant complex wore outsized hats meant to evoke Uncle Sam and took play money from the people dressed as Philip Morris cigarettes.
INFACT claims that Philip Morris employs more than 240 lobbyists to influence federal and state government officials.
A spokeswoman for Philip Morris said the INFACT protestors were welcome to voice their opinions.

Philip Morris chief executive Geoffrey Bible was expected to be questioned at the shareholders meeting about secret talks between cigarette makers and U.S. anti-tobacco forces about a possible sweeping resolution of hundreds of lawsuits filed on behalf of sick smokers.
Sources close to the talks have said the tobacco industry may pay as much as $300 billion or more over 25 years as part of a deal.
